# B--

> B-- is a small, fully defined programming language with a strict C99
> bytecode interpreter and a Python reference implementation. The language
> specification is frozen at version 1.0.0. Repository release 17.14 updates
> documentation and discoverability without changing language behavior.

## Canonical facts

- Name: B-- (pronounced "be minus minus").
- Repository: https://github.com/erluza/bmm-lang
- License: MIT.
- Types: int (32-bit signed, wraparound), str (immutable byte sequence),
  arr (mutable, zero-indexed, bounds-checked).
- Keywords: let fn if else loop break ret use and or not end.
- Built-ins: print println input len push pop str int chr ord sub arr exit
  argv clock.
- Execution: source is compiled to bytecode for a stack-based virtual machine.
- Memory: mark-and-sweep garbage collector.
- Portability: all operating-system access is isolated in src/pal/pal.h.
- Reference implementation: ref/bmm.py, Python standard library only.
- C implementation: C99, no external libraries.

## Getting started

- Build: `make`
- Test: `make test`
- Install: `make install PREFIX="$HOME/.local"`
- Run: `bmm file.bmm`
- REPL: `bmm`
- Compile: `bmm build file.bmm -o file.bmc`
- Run bytecode: `bmm run file.bmc`

## Verification

- Gate output: https://github.com/erluza/bmm-lang/blob/main/docs/GATE_OUTPUT.txt
- Verification report: https://github.com/erluza/bmm-lang/blob/main/docs/VERIFICATION_REPORT.md
- The gate covers 18 stages, 20 conformance programs mapped to 25 rules,
  15 examples, 2,000 differential fuzz programs, 1,000 random or truncated
  sources, 500 corrupt .bmc files, 34 mutations, and 20 regression probes.

## Citation

Use CITATION.cff: https://github.com/erluza/bmm-lang/blob/main/CITATION.cff

## Limits

- Parser nesting is limited to 1000 levels.
- Nested functions that capture outer locals are rejected at compile time.
- Bytecode version 2 is required; version 1 files are rejected.
- argv is a value, not a function; argv() is a compile-time error.
